questions.questionTextEn: How many ways can a product of 4 matrices `A1 · A2 · A3 · A4` be fully parenthesized?
questions.explanationEn: The number of full parenthesizations of n matrices is the Catalan number `C_{n-1}`. For n = 4, `C_3 = 5`.

questions.questionTextEn: A valid topological ordering of a DAG can be obtained by running DFS and ordering the vertices in:
questions.explanationEn: In a DAG, for every directed edge u -> v, vertex v finishes before u. Sorting vertices by decreasing finish time guarantees u appears before v.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following sorting algorithms has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity AND is in-place (O(1) auxiliary space)?
questions.explanationEn: Heap Sort runs in O(n log n) worst-case time and uses O(1) extra space. Merge Sort requires O(n) extra space, Quick Sort has O(n^2) worst case, and Insertion Sort is O(n^2).

questions.questionTextEn: Huffman coding produces an optimal prefix-free binary code. What is the time complexity to build a Huffman tree for `n` characters using a binary min-heap?
questions.explanationEn: Building the initial heap takes O(n), followed by n - 1 iterations each doing two Extract-Min and one Insert operation in O(log n), totaling O(n log n).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following correctly orders the functions in strictly increasing order of asymptotic growth rate?
questions.explanationEn: Polynomial `n^1.5` dominates `n log n`, exponential `2^n` dominates any polynomial, and factorial `n!` (by Stirling's approximation ~`(n/e)^n`) dominates `2^n`.

questions.questionTextEn: How many inversions (pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `A[i] > A[j]`) exist in the array `[4, 1, 3, 2]`?
questions.explanationEn: Inversion pairs are `(4, 1)`, `(4, 3)`, `(4, 2)`, and `(3, 2)` — a total of 4 inversions.

questions.questionTextEn: If problem A is NP-complete and problem B is in NP such that A is polynomial-time reducible to B (A <=_p B), then:
questions.explanationEn: Since every problem in NP reduces to A and A <=_p B, by transitivity every problem in NP reduces to B (so B is NP-hard). Together with B in NP, B is NP-complete.

questions.questionTextEn: How many edges are in a Minimum Spanning Tree of a connected weighted undirected graph with 15 vertices and 42 edges?
questions.explanationEn: Every spanning tree of a connected graph on V vertices has exactly V - 1 = 15 - 1 = 14 edges.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the length of the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) of the strings `"ABCBDAB"` and `"BDCABA"`?
questions.explanationEn: Common subsequences of maximum length 4 include `"BCBA"`, `"BDAB"`, and `"BCAB"`. No common subsequence of length 5 exists.

questions.questionTextEn: Assuming P != NP, which of the following statements are TRUE?
optionsEn: No NP-complete problem can be solved in polynomial time
Every problem in P is also in NP
Every NP-hard problem belongs to NP
If any NP-complete problem has a polynomial-time algorithm, then P = NP
questions.explanationEn: P is a subset of NP (B). If P != NP, no NP-complete problem is in P (A), and solving any NP-complete problem in P would collapse P = NP (D). NP-hard problems need not be in NP — e.g., the Halting Problem (C is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about shortest-path algorithms are TRUE?
optionsEn: BFS computes single-source shortest paths in an unweighted graph in O(V + E) time
Bellman-Ford correctly handles graphs with negative edge weights provided there is no reachable negative cycle
Floyd-Warshall can detect a negative-weight cycle by checking if any diagonal entry `dist[i][i] < 0` after completion
Dijkstra's algorithm always fails whenever a graph has a cycle
questions.explanationEn: BFS finds unweighted shortest paths in O(V + E) (A), Bellman-Ford handles negative edges without negative cycles (B), and Floyd-Warshall flags negative cycles via `dist[i][i] < 0` (C). Dijkstra handles positive-weight cycles without issue (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: How many subsets of `{2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10}` have elements that sum to exactly 10?
questions.explanationEn: The subsets summing to 10 are `{10}`, `{2, 8}`, and `{2, 3, 5}` — a total of 3 subsets.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following recurrences have the tight asymptotic solution `Θ(n log n)`?
questions.explanationEn: A and D match Master Theorem Case 2 -> `Θ(n log n)`. In B, every level of the recursion tree sums to `n` and depth is `O(log n)` -> `Θ(n log n)`. In C, `n^(log2 4) = n^2` dominates `n`, giving `Θ(n^2)` (C is false).

questions.questionTextEn: What is the length of the Longest Palindromic Subsequence (LPS) of the string `"BBABCBCAB"`?
questions.explanationEn: One longest palindromic subsequence is `"BABCBAB"`, which has length 7.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the recurrence `T(n) = 8T(n/2) + n^2`. Its tight solution is `Θ(n^k)`. What is the value of `k`?
questions.explanationEn: Here `a = 8, b = 2`, so `n^(log_2 8) = n^3`. Since `f(n) = n^2 = O(n^(3 - 1))`, Case 1 of Master Theorem gives `T(n) = Θ(n^3)`, so `k = 3`.

questions.questionTextEn: Six characters have frequencies: a: 5, b: 9, c: 12, d: 13, e: 16, f: 45. What is the total number of bits required to encode a 100-character message with these exact frequencies using an optimal Huffman code?
Which of the following statements about Breadth-First Search (BFS) on an undirected graph G starting from vertex `s` are TRUE?
optionsEn: Every edge `(u, v)` in G connects vertices whose BFS distances from `s` differ by at most 1
G is bipartite if and only if no edge connects two vertices at the same BFS level
BFS always produces a Minimum Spanning Tree on a weighted graph
The BFS tree contains a shortest path (in number of edges) from `s` to every reachable vertex
questions.explanationEn: In undirected BFS, edges only connect same-level or adjacent-level vertices (A); same-level edges create odd cycles, obstructing bipartiteness (B); and BFS trees capture unweighted shortest paths (D). BFS ignores edge weights, so C is false.

questions.questionTextEn: A sorted array of 31 elements is searched using binary search. What is the maximum number of key comparisons required to find an element (assuming 1 equality/ordering check per probe)?
questions.explanationEn: 31 = 2^5 - 1 forms a perfect binary search tree of 5 levels, so at most `floor(log2(31)) + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5` probes are needed.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the maximum sum of any non-empty contiguous subarray of `[-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4]`?
questions.explanationEn: The contiguous subarray `[4, -1, 2, 1]` has sum `4 - 1 + 2 + 1 = 6`, which is the maximum.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about Dynamic Programming (DP) are TRUE?
optionsEn: DP is effective when a problem exhibits both optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems
Top-down memoization computes only the subproblems actually needed for the given input
Bottom-up tabulation avoids recursion call-stack overhead
DP always achieves a strictly faster worst-case time complexity than greedy algorithms on the same problem
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C accurately describe DP. When a greedy choice property holds (e.g., Activity Selection or Fractional Knapsack), greedy algorithms are typically faster than DP (D is false).
